record.context_brief: Removing o(m) from judicious bisection bound
record.original_question: Let k be a positive integer. Can the o(m) term be removed from Lee et al.’s bisection theorem, so that every graph with m edges and minimum degree 2k or 2k + 1 has a bisection (S, T) satisfying max{e(S), e(T)} <= ((k + 1)/(2(2k + 1)))m?

evidence.quote:
Theorem 3.3[40] Every graph with m edges and minimum degree 2k or 2k + 1 admits a bisection (S, S) such that
max{e(S), e(S)} ≤ ( k + 1
2(2k + 1) + o(1) ) m.
Problem 3.3[40] Is it possible to remove the tail term o(m) in Theorem 3.3?

Following Theorem 3.4, one sees that if a graph G with m edges and minimum degree at least 2k or 2k + 1 does not admit bisection of which each class induces a subgraph with at most k+1
2(2k+1)m edges, then G is a sparse graph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a positive integer. A bisection of a graph $G=(V,E)$ on $n$ vertices is an ordered partition $(S,T)$ of $V$ into two parts with $\bigl||S|-|T|\bigr|\le 1$. For a vertex set $U\subseteq V$, let $e(U)$ denote the number of edges of $G$ with both endpoints in $U$. It is known that every graph $G$ with $m$ edges and minimum degree at least $2k$ or $2k+1$ admits a bisection $(S,T)$ satisfying
$$\max\{e(S),e(T)\}\le\left(\frac{k+1}{2(2k+1)}+o(1)\right)m,$$
where $o(1)\to 0$ as $m\to\infty$.

Determine whether the $o(1)$ error term can be removed. That is, decide whether every graph with $m$ edges and minimum degree at least $2k$ (respectively at least $2k+1$) admits a bisection $(S,T)$ with
$$\max\{e(S),e(T)\}\le\frac{k+1}{2(2k+1)}\,m.$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the bisection result giving the bound $\bigl(\tfrac{k+1}{2(2k+1)}+o(1)\bigr)m$ for graphs of minimum degree $2k$ or $2k+1$, but did not turn up any paper removing the $o(m)$ term. The question is posed as an open problem in the partitioning literature and no resolution was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: On judicious bisections of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Bisection of graphs with minimum degree at least 2k or 2k+1 admits a bisection with max{e(S),e(T)} <= ((k+1)/(2(2k+1)) + o(1)) m.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the bisection bound with the additive o(m) tail term that the question asks to remove.

status_evidence.title: Bisections of graphs (Lee, Loh, Sudakov)
status_evidence.snippet: Bisections of graphs with prescribed minimum degree, with judicious bounds of the form (1/(2(2k+1)/(k+1)) + o(1)) m.
status_evidence.claim: Source of the theorem whose o(1) term is the object of the open question.
